chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Muhammad from some of our companions from Muhammad ibn 'Isa ibn 'Ubayd from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Muzanni from 'Imran al-Zafarani who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'The sky is overcast upon us in Iraq today, and the next two days, and the third. Which day should we fast?' He said, 'Look to the day you fasted in the previous year, and fast the fifth day.'
ai.seo_question: How to determine the first day of fasting in Ramadan when the sky is cloudy in Iraq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) addresses the practical challenge of determining the start of Ramadan in Iraq during prolonged overcast conditions (*istikmal*), where the moon cannot be visually confirmed. He instructs the companion to rely on *istikmal* (completing thirty days) by counting from the day he fasted in the previous year, establishing the fifth day as the start. This ruling highlights the Shia reliance on calculated lunar cycles and continuity of practice when direct observation is obstructed, distinguishing it from the Sunni emphasis on communal sighting in such scenarios. The method ensures unity in fasting by anchoring the new month to the individual's established rhythm of worship.
